Subject: Compliance recap: SOC 2 timeline, questionnaire & cloud mapping

Hi Olivia — great conversation this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on your procurement timeline.

Key takeaways from the demo/discovery:
- FinLytics requires SOC 2 Type II evidence and proof of GDPR data handling before legal signs off.
- Primary data flow: customer PII is sent to our API for inference; results may be stored in customer-owned S3 or Redwoods-managed ephemeral storage depending on environment.
- FinLytics is evaluating both our hosted API and Dedicated (VPC) options — you flagged encryption-in-transit and HSM/KMS controls as blockers for hosted.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) I will kick off the vendor security questionnaire — attaching a short stub to capture any missing fields. Can you confirm the procurement contact who will own this?
2) We’ll provide our current subprocessor inventory (cloud infra, observability, logging, analytics) and high-level data boundary map for the two deployment options by EOD tomorrow.
3) Our SOC 2 Type II report (last completed audit) is attached for your review; let us know if you need an NDA-first exchange.

Timelines (proposed):
- Questionnaire completion: FinLytics completes and returns by Fri 2026-08-13
- Subprocessor inventory and cloud boundary diagram: Redwood delivers by Wed 2026-08-12
- Legal / procurement review window: target sign-off by 2026-08-25 (flexible)

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire_FinLytics_20260811.docx, soc2-type2-report-redwood-2025.pdf

If that looks right I’ll loop in our security owner and Marissa to produce the inventory and a one-page cloud map.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Compliance recap: SOC 2 timeline, questionnaire & cloud mapping

Hi Olivia — attaching the subprocessor inventory CSV and a brief cloud-data boundary summary. High-level answers here for procurement.

Subprocessor highlights (summary):
- Cloud compute & storage: AWS (us-east-1) — EC2, EBS, S3. Data boundary: request payloads processed on EC2; customer-configured S3 used for persistent storage in Dedicated deployments only.
- Model hosting & autoscaling: GCP (us-central1) for burst in certain regions — we can avoid cross-cloud bursts if required.
- Observability & logging: Datadog (log ingestion only; retention configurable per customer). Logs containing identifiers are only retained if enabled; default is scrubbing.
- Secrets/KMS: AWS KMS / GCP KMS; Dedicated supports customer-managed HSM/KMS; hosted supports BYOK for enterprise tiers.
- CDNs & distribution: Fastly (edge caching for static assets only; no inference payloads cached).
- Analytics: Segment (eventing) used for product-usage telemetry — PII-only if customer opts in (off by default).

Data sharing boundaries:
- Hosted API (default): request/response handled in our hosted pool; we do not persist PII by default. Telemetry/usage events are pseudonymized; customers must opt into richer analytics.
- Dedicated / VPC: all processing remains inside customer VPC / peered network; persistent artifacts (logs, metrics) can be routed to customer-owned S3/Cloud Storage and customer KMS.

Attached files: redwood_subprocessors_inventory_20260811.csv, soc2-type2-report-redwood-2025.pdf

If you prefer, we can produce a redlined version of your questionnaire with answers inline (I can push that by EOB today). Also happy to set a short follow-up with our security team to walk procurement through the KMS/HSM steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Security Partnerships | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
